meta.description: Decompose total effects into direct and indirect paths through mediators using observational mediation, CMAverse 4-way decomposition, HIMA/HIMA2, BAMA, two-step or MVMR mediation, and double-ML mediation.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: All numerical results came from fresh synthetic data and installed-package output; no clinical or literature facts were invented.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Scope section correctly declined an individual statin-dose decision and directed the request to a prescribing clinician.

methodological_ground.detail: The tested workflows require sensitivity analysis, instrument-strength checks, and warnings for weak instruments or unmeasured confounding.

code_usability.detail: All shipped R files parse. Fresh analyses produced checked values or parseable output files; package exit 139 is reproduced by minimal package loads and is an environment issue, not a Skill-code failure.

functional_suitability.note: Covers the advertised observational, interaction, high-dimensional, MR, and double-ML regimes with runnable routes or an explicit OpenGWAS-authenticated sketch.

reliability.note: Common Errors gives concrete recovery paths for HIMA, medDML, MVMR, and sensitivity failures; the live OpenGWAS route remains token-gated.

performance_context.note: The concise SKILL.md routes advanced material into focused references and a dedicated HIMA script.

agent_usability.note: Decision tree, thresholds, reporting checklist, and method-specific pointers make the workflow clear from a cold start.

human_usability.note: Natural prompt examples and a compact usage guide are supplied; selecting among several causal estimands still requires substantive expertise.

security.note: No secrets or destructive operations appear, and Scope instructs de-identification; the R CLI necessarily accepts user file paths without a sandbox.

maintainability.note: The 257-line entrypoint has explicit reference routing, executable examples, and a separate parameterized HIMA script.

agent_specific.note: Trigger language is precise and the Scope section supplies a clinical escape hatch; the authenticated OpenGWAS sketch is intentionally not executable offline.

recommendations.title: Repair shared R package exit-139 behavior
recommendations.problem: mediation, TwoSampleMR, and HIMA can finish valid computations and then exit 139 in the supplied R runtime, even for a one-line library load.
recommendations.root_cause: The failure is reproduced without Skill code, so it belongs to the shared runtime or compiled package stack rather than this Skill.
recommendations.fix: Audit-environment owner should repair or rebuild the affected R package/runtime stack and repeat the smoke tests. No change to this Skill is indicated by the evidence.
